fields.name: live_data_bank
fields.meaning: Bank 0 of the save memory is the program's own working data area (its data segment points here), kept alive by the battery. Settings, the current-app choice and other state are read and changed in place; there is no separate 'save' copy step for them
fields.evidence: code fe01:0105 (interrupt entry sets data segment 1000 = bank 0), fe01:01B3 (boot reads settings straight from bank 0); play diff (a setting changes in bank 0 the moment its row is toggled)

fields.name: unused_head
fields.meaning: Not used; zero in every state
fields.evidence: diff of boot, early and finished play states (always 0)

fields.name: memory_tables
fields.meaning: Tables written at the first start-up: repeating 4-byte entries (address word + 0x2c20/0x2e20/0x1220 tags); look like the program's memory-block tables
fields.evidence: boot->first-play diff (written at first start-up, unchanged after)

fields.name: unknown_work_1
fields.meaning: Program working data; single bytes change with menu moves (0x02da follows the main-menu cursor)
fields.evidence: play diffs across menu moves

fields.name: dialog_image_buffer
fields.meaning: Picture buffer for the pop-up toolbar/dialog graphics (used part 0x3f20-0x4624, rest zero); filled when a dialog opens, cleared when it closes
fields.evidence: play diff (dialog opened: patterned bytes appear, then cleared)

fields.name: screen_buffer
fields.meaning: Screen picture, one bit per pixel, 28 bytes per row (224 dots wide); changes on every screen redraw
fields.evidence: play diff (only the toggled option's pixels change)

fields.name: unknown_work_2
fields.meaning: Program working data (0x67c2-0x6b7d, 0x7ecd-0x7efa and 0x90a6-0x90e8 are written at first start-up and on menu changes)
fields.evidence: boot->first-play and menu diffs

fields.name: settings_screen_state
fields.meaning: State of the Settings screen while it is open: dialog state (0xda6e), return screen (0xda70, copied to 0xfb21 on confirm), cursor row (0xda71), number of rows (0xda73 = 7)
fields.evidence: code lin EFAC1 (screen setup writes da71/da73/da85/da86), lin EFD24 (confirm copies da70 to fb21); play diff on opening Settings

fields.name: unknown_work_4
fields.meaning: Program working data; zero in observed states
fields.evidence: diff (zero in all states)

fields.name: record_pointer_table
fields.meaning: 21 far pointers (offset + segment 0x1000) to records of 0x42 bytes starting at 0xe4b8 (e4b8, e4fa, e53c, ...); written at first start-up; what the records hold was not identified
fields.evidence: boot->first-play diff; pointer stride 0x42 verified in bytes

fields.name: unknown_records
fields.meaning: Area the pointer table points into (0x42-byte records); all zero in observed states
fields.evidence: diff (zero in all states)

fields.name: version_stamp
fields.meaning: Text 'WonderGate 1.0.1_04302' (22 chars, NUL-padded). Checked at every power-on; if it does not match, all eight banks of the save memory are wiped and the factory settings are written
fields.evidence: code fe01:01EB (compare vs ROM copy), fe01:030A (wipe banks 0-7, write stamp, defaults fe01:04A7); boot->first-play diff

fields.name: image_display
fields.meaning: Settings: image display (show pictures on web pages). 1 = show (factory value), 0 = hide. Copied to the console memory at power-on
fields.evidence: verified natural save; play diff (1->0 the moment the row is toggled, before confirming); code lin EFE49 (toggle: xor word 0xeeb8,1), fe01:04BE (default 1), fe01:021D (boot copy to 0000:0c00)

fields.name: image_display_hi
fields.meaning: High byte of the image setting (written as a 16-bit word); always 0
fields.evidence: code fe01:04BE (word write), lin EFE49; diff (always 0)

fields.name: text_encoding
fields.meaning: Settings value for preferred web-page text encoding: 0 = S-JIS, 1 = EUC, 2 = automatic (factory default). A cold-boot clone selecting 0 or 1 reaches and displays that choice on the Settings screen; this does not establish which decoder is used for page content.
fields.evidence: Power-on copies SRAM 0xEEBA to console RAM 0000:0C01 at FE01:0229. Selector cycle and store are mapped at E82B:7997 / linear EFC44 and sibling handlers; default is set at FE01:04C4. Native cloned saves 2→0 and 2→1 reached the verified Settings route; selector output and WRAM changed. No checksum repair applied. The run did not identify a page decoder consumer or verify rendered S-JIS/EUC text.

fields.name: landscape_screen_size
fields.meaning: Settings: screen size when the console is held sideways. 0 = 1 screen (factory value), 1 = 2 screens
fields.evidence: natural saves (0->1 when 2 screens chosen; unchanged when only picture size changed); code lin EFE68 (toggle: xor word 0xeebb,1), fe01:04CF (default 0)

fields.name: image_size
fields.meaning: Settings: picture size. 0 = 50% (factory value), 1 = 100%
fields.evidence: natural saves (0->1 with 100% chosen, 1->0 with 50% chosen); code lin EFE7A (toggle: xor word 0xeebd,1), fe01:04C9 (default 0)

fields.name: home_page
fields.meaning: Settings: home page address, zero-terminated text; factory value www.mopera.ne.jp/
fields.evidence: code fe01:04D5 (default copy from ROM); shown on the Settings screen; boot->first-play diff

fields.name: dial_number
fields.meaning: Settings: access point phone number, zero-terminated text; factory value #9601
fields.evidence: code fe01:04E5 (default from ROM); shown on the Settings screen

fields.name: ppp_user_id
fields.meaning: Settings > connection settings: dial-up user name, zero-terminated text; empty by default
fields.evidence: code fe01:04F5 (default empty from ROM), readers lin F0713/F07C6/F083E; sub-screen lists user ID then password; never edited in play

fields.name: ppp_password
fields.meaning: Settings > connection settings: dial-up password, zero-terminated text; empty by default
fields.evidence: code fe01:0505 (default empty from ROM), readers lin F0769/F07D6/F0875; sub-screen order; never edited in play

fields.name: server_name_1
fields.meaning: Server host name, factory value bpl02.mopera.ne.jp; rewritten with the same text at every power-on, so a stored change would not last
fields.evidence: code fe01:0515 (default), fe01:029F (rewritten at every boot)

fields.name: server_name_2
fields.meaning: Second server host name, factory value bpl01.mopera.ne.jp; also rewritten at every power-on
fields.evidence: code fe01:0525 (default), fe01:02AF (rewritten at every boot)

fields.name: connection_numbers
fields.meaning: Group of small numbers set with the connection defaults: words 0xf0d5=0, 0xf0d7=0, 0xf0d9=8, 0xf0db=0, 0xf0df=0, 0xf0e1=0, byte 0xf0e3=12; 0xf0dd is never written by the defaults routine (0 after a factory wipe); meanings not identified
fields.evidence: code fe01:0550-0574 (defaults; no write to 0xf0dd); readers lin F3D4C, FC839 (0xf0d9), lin F1C0A, FC567 (0xf0e3); values verified in every finished save

fields.name: connection_texts_a
fields.meaning: Six empty text fields (four of 0x21 bytes at 0xf0e4/0xf105/0xf126/0xf147, two of 0x61 at 0xf168/0xf1c9), then host names ns2.channel.or.jp (0xf22a, 0x61 bytes) and ns1.channel.or.jp (0xf28b, 0x61 bytes), a flag word 0xf2ec = 1 and an empty 0x21-byte text at 0xf2ee; probably mail account settings
fields.evidence: code fe01:0582-0615 (defaults incl. ROM host names fe01:047E/0490); console memory 0000:0c10 holds a pointer to 0xf0e4; layout confirmed, meanings guessed

fields.name: connection_texts_b
fields.meaning: Second group: zero block 0xf30f (0x11 bytes), empty texts 0xf320 (0x21) and 0xf341 (0xe7), flag word 0xf428 = 1, empty texts 0xf42a and 0xf48b (0x61 bytes each)
fields.evidence: code fe01:061E-0671 (defaults); console memory 0000:0c14 holds a pointer to 0xf30f; layout confirmed, meanings guessed

fields.name: settings_undo_copy
fields.meaning: Copy of the whole settings record 0xeeb8-0xf4eb taken when the Settings screen opens; copied back if the player cancels
fields.evidence: code lin EFAC1 (copy 0x634 bytes 0xeeb8 -> 0xf4ec on entry), lin EFE1A (copy back on cancel); play diff (snapshot appears on open, byte-identical to the record)

fields.name: current_app
fields.meaning: App currently running (0 = main menu, 1 = BROWSER, 2 = MAILER, 3 = downloaded game). Always reset to 0 (main menu) at power-on, so the stored value never affects boot; used by the menu loop to pick which part runs next
fields.evidence: code fe01:00A0 (jump table on 0xfb20 with targets menu/browser/mailer/game), fe01:02DB/00CF/1E52 (reset to 0); play diff (0->1 on entering BROWSER); finished saves storing 1 still boot to the main menu

fields.name: return_screen
fields.meaning: Screen to return to after the Settings screen is confirmed
fields.evidence: code lin EFD24 (copy from 0xda70); play diff on confirm

fields.name: boot_vars
fields.meaning: Variables re-set at every power-on (0xfb2a = 1, 0xfb32 far pointer 20f7:1df0, 0xfb41 = 6, 0xfb49 far pointer 20f7:1fb0, others 0); no saved meaning

fields.name: boot_cleared
fields.meaning: Cleared at every power-on; no saved meaning
fields.evidence: code fe01:0204

fields.name: unknown_work_3
fields.meaning: Program working data; zero in observed states (0xfd92 cleared at every power-on)
fields.evidence: code fe01:0215; diff

fields.name: live_checksum
fields.meaning: Check word of bank 0, written only by the checksummed backup routine; zero in every observed state
fields.evidence: code fe01:1CBB (writes it, then copies the bank to the backup); diff (always 0)

fields.name: unused_tail
fields.meaning: Not used; zero
fields.evidence: diff (always 0)

fields.name: banks_1_3
fields.meaning: Banks 1-3: wiped at factory reset, not written in observed play; bank 2 is where a downloaded game is copied to before it runs
fields.evidence: code fe01:030A (wipe), fe01:1E0E (copy bank 7 -> bank 2 and run it); diff (zero)

fields.name: bank_4
fields.meaning: Bank 4: two 8-byte block headers written at first start-up (0x40102, 0x48a02); probably storage for mail or downloaded pages
fields.evidence: diff (only these 16 bytes appear at first start-up)

fields.name: bank_5
fields.meaning: Bank 5: wiped at factory reset, not written in observed play
fields.evidence: code fe01:030A; diff (zero)

fields.name: backup_copy
fields.meaning: Bank 6: backup copy of bank 0 (bytes 0x10-0xfff1 copied as they are). Refreshed when the Settings screen is confirmed and at every power-on; restored over bank 0 at power-on only if its check word matches
fields.evidence: code fe01:1C40 (refresh, called from Settings confirm lin EFD2F), fe01:1691 (bank-to-bank copy), fe01:1D3C (power-on check / restore); play diffs (bank 6 becomes bank 0 except post-confirm bytes)

fields.name: backup_checksum
fields.meaning: Check word of the backup: 16-bit sum of low16(word x its offset) for all words at offsets 0x10-0xffee. The usual refresh routine computes it and then overwrites it with bank 0's word at 0xfff0 (zero), so in finished saves it is 0 and fails the power-on check; the game then keeps bank 0 and refreshes the backup
fields.evidence: recomputed over all 162 save images: 3 non-trivial matches (0x658c twice, 0x08dc once), 110 empty-backup matches, 49 fail-by-design; mid-refresh captures differ from bank 0 only at 0xfff0; code fe01:1C40/1D3C

fields.name: backup_tail
fields.meaning: Not used
fields.evidence: diff (zero)

fields.name: bank_7_download
fields.meaning: Bank 7: room for a downloaded game; one is run at start-up when the bank begins with the text SWAN. Empty in observed play
fields.evidence: code fe01:1DD7 (compare 'SWAN' fe01:1DD2, copy 0xfff0 bytes to bank 2, jump 1000:0010); diff (zero)

fields.name: console_eeprom
fields.meaning: Not used by this game: unchanged from the console's own data in all states
fields.evidence: diff of all 162 play states' EEPROM vs boot (identical)

values.value: top-level checksum_ok is the backup block's: the outcome of the game's own power-on check. Finished saves normally fail it by design (the refresh overwrites the stored word with 0) and the game keeps bank 0. The live-bank word is written by fe01:1CBB but never checked by any code path.
reset to main menu at every power-on
bank 0 word at 0xFFF0; written only by fe01:1CBB
bank 6 copy of bank 0; checked at every boot
this game never reads or writes the internal EEPROM; every save leaves it identical to the console default
unknown image size (want 0x80000 SRAM or 0x80 EEPROM)

left.value: fix needs a 0x80000-byte SRAM image (got %d bytes)

values.value: a fixed backup passes the boot check, so the game would restore bank 6 over bank 0 at power-on
